text.p: Indian term-lender the Industrial Credit and Investment Corp of India (ICICI) said late on Thursday it had launched its $150-million Yankee bond issue with a 7.75 percent coupon rate.
ICICI said in a statement the bonds were of 10-year maturity and issued as a Rule 144A offering under its global term note programme.
This was the second issue under the programme, the first being a $100 million issue of floating rate notes in March 1997, it said.
The issue was led by J.P. Morgan as book runner and Merrill Lynch as joint lead with Salomon Brothers and Morgan Stanley Dean Witter as co-managers, the statement said.
ICICI said the issue received good response from investors all over the world and 70 percent was placed in the U.S., 20 percent in Europe and the rest in Asia.
ICICI is India's second largest term lending bank after the Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI).
